subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Swarm Robotics: Strength in Numbers
description: A quick, practical guide to Swarm Robotics: Strength in Numbers.

hook.text: A thousand tiny robots cooperate to build a structure. No leader tells them what to do. They follow local rules only.

buildup.text: Each robot senses only its neighbors. Simple rules like 'follow the one ahead' and 'avoid collisions' create group behavior.

discovery.text: Harvard's Kilobot project showed 1,000 robots self-assembling into shapes using only infrared signals between neighbors.

twist.text: If one robot fails, the swarm adapts. No single point of failure. Redundancy is built into the numbers.

climax.text: Swarm drones survey farmland, search disaster zones, and could one day build structures on Mars without human supervision.

punchline.text: One robot is fragile. A thousand are unstoppable.

quiz.question: How do swarm robots coordinate without a central controller?
options: They receive commands from a satellite link that manages the whole group
Each robot follows simple local rules based only on nearby neighbors
One designated leader robot sends instructions to all others wirelessly
